title: A sequential methodology for integral evaluation of motor and non-motor behaviors in parkinsonian rodents
author: Soto-Rojas, Bañuelos, et al.
materials: 1.Animals were anesthetized with a mixture of 100 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg xylazine injected intraperitoneally.2.They were placed on a stereotaxic frame (Stoelting; Wood Dale, IL, USA), and the skull was trepanned with the following coordinates for BSSG administration in the left substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc): anteroposterior (AP), +2.1 mm from interaural midpoint; medial-lateral (ML), +2.0 mm from interparietal suture; and dorsal-ventral (DV), −6.8 mm from dura mater [3,14]. The coordinates for 6-OHDA administration in the left striatum were: AP, +7.7 mm; ML, +4.0 mm; and DV, −5.4 [15].Note: It is important that the dura mater is broken for the correct neurotoxin diffusion. It can be done with the tip of a hypodermic needle.3.BSSG (Daucosterol; MedChemExpress) was administered at a concentration of 6 µg/µl DMSO (Sigma- Aldrich; St. Louis, MO, USA), or only 1 µl of DMSO (mock group). The concentration of 6-OHDA (Sigma- Aldrich; St. Louis, MO, USA) was 20 µg free base in 3 µL of PBS containing 0.2% ascorbic acid (Sigma-Aldrich; St. Louis, MO, USA). These neurotoxins were independently injected using a microperfusion pump (Stoelting; Wood Dale, IL, USA) to maintain a flow rate of 0.13 µL/min.Note: We recommend using a blunt 20-gauge dental needle, so that the diffusion of the neurotoxin remains in a radial direction, conversely to the bevel orientation. Once the infusion is finished, wait between 5 and 10 min to allow the complete and appropriate neurotoxin diffusion.4.The wound was sutured with silk 00 and treated with a mixture of oxytetracycline and polymyxin B (Pfizer; Toluca, Mexico) to prevent infections.Note: Before performing stereotaxic surgeries, it is a good practice to verify the coordinates and the lesion site by dye-staining, i.e., by injecting Evans blue dye (Sigma-Aldrich; St. Louis, MO, USA) in 95% of ethanol.
Step 2: Behavioral tests of parkinsonian rodents

Rodents can be housed individually or in groups; however, once defined the scheme, it should be maintained to avoid behavior changes. Since rodents are social animals, single housing may affect the results in several behavioral tests validated herein. Undesirable effects from isolation are anxiety-like behavior, changes in neurochemical functions, and hyperactivity [16]. On this basis, it is preferable to use group housing. Also, rodents should be daily handled for a few minutes for habituation purposes (at least 5 days before the behavioral tests), since stress can modify the results.

1.On the pre-test day, animals must be transferred to the room where the test will be carried out at least 1 h before, to avoid stress.2.Fill in the swimming cylinders with water at a depth of approximately 30 cm (Fig. 6a) for rats and 15 cm for mice.3.The temperature must be between 22–24 °C. Water temperature can be monitored with a mercury thermometer.Note: The range of temperature between 22 and 24 °C is habitual in most laboratories and allows to maintain a constant temperature for water. Lower temperatures could lead to animals’ hypothermia, possibly affecting their activity [25].4.Place animals individually in the swim cylinders for 15 min. After this time, remove rodents from water and dry them as best as possible with microfiber towels. Return them to their cages, providing heat through a lamp.Note: If rodents are housed in a group, those subjected to the swim pre-test should not be mixed with unevaluated rodents, since their encounter can cause them stress. Therefore, it is advisable to house the animal temporary (2 h) in a separate cage, and then regroup it according to the experimental condition.5.Water changes between each evaluation must be done, keeping the same depth and temperature, as mentioned above.6.Refill the swim cylinders 24 h after the pre-test, before placing rodents in them. Start the video recording, ensuring the full duration of the test.Note: We recommend recording the test directly, above and alongside the swim cylinders. Also, ensure image quality (clarity and sharpness) to allow proper evaluation and distinction of individual behaviors.7.Place the rodents in the swim cylinder for 5 min. After this time has passed, dry animals and put them back in their cages.Note: A lateral view of the swim cylinder adequately evidences rodent immobility behavior (Supplementary video 6).

steps.title: Perform stereotaxic neurotoxin injection
steps.instruction: Anesthetize each rat with 100 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg xylazine (i.p.), secure in a Stoelting stereotaxic frame, trepan the skull and break the dura with a hypodermic needle, then inject the chosen neurotoxin at the specified coordinates using a blunt 20‑gauge dental needle and a micro‑perfusion pump at 0.13 µL/min; wait 5–10 min after infusion, close the wound with silk 00 sutures, apply a mixture of oxytetracycline and polymyxin B, and optionally verify coordinates by injecting Evans blue dye in 95 % ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Prepare anesthesia: 100 mg/kg ketamine + 10 mg/kg xylazine, i.p.
Place animal in stereotaxic frame (Stoelting).
Drill skull at target site.
Break dura mater with tip of a hypodermic needle.
For BSSG lesions, use left SNpc coordinates: AP +2.1 mm (interaural midpoint), ML +2.0 mm (interparietal suture), DV −6.8 mm from dura.
For 6‑OHDA lesions, use left striatum coordinates: AP +7.7 mm, ML +4.0 mm, DV −5.4 mm.
Prepare BSSG solution: 6 µg/µL DMSO (or 1 µL DMSO for mock).
Prepare 6‑OHDA solution: 20 µg free base in 3 µL PBS with 0.2 % ascorbic acid.
Load solution into micro‑perfusion pump (Stoelting) and inject at 0.13 µL/min using a blunt 20‑gauge dental needle.
After infusion, wait 5–10 min before needle withdrawal to allow diffusion.
Suture wound with silk 00.
Apply topical oxytetracycline + polymyxin B mixture.
Optional: inject Evans blue dye in 95 % ethanol to confirm target location before actual surgeries.

steps.title: Prepare behavioral testing environment
steps.instruction: House rats in groups (unless otherwise required), handle each animal for a few minutes daily for at least 5 days before testing, keep cages at 90 % of free‑feeding body weight, clean all devices and surfaces with 30 % ethanol between evaluations, change water after each forced‑swim trial, and follow the 7‑day test sequence (Day 1 open field, Day 2 vibrissae + olfactory pre‑test, Day 3 olfactory test, Day 4 uncoordinated gait, Day 5 cylinder, Day 6 forced‑swim pre‑test, Day 7 forced‑swim test). Train for the gait test 2 h before the Day 4 evaluation on Days 2 and 3, and ensure at least 45 days between repeated test batteries or use a new cohort.

substeps.instruction: Maintain group housing; avoid single housing unless necessary.
Handle each rat 5 min daily for ≥5 days before first test.
Keep animals at ~90 % of free‑feeding weight throughout.
Disinfect apparatus with 30 % ethanol between each animal.
For forced‑swim, replace water after each animal.
Follow test schedule:
Day 1 – Open field
Day 2 – Vibrissae test + Olfactory asymmetry pre‑test
Day 3 – Olfactory asymmetry test
Day 4 – Uncoordinated gait test
Day 5 – Cylinder test
Day 6 – Forced‑swim pre‑test
Day 7 – Forced‑swim test
Train animals for gait test 2 h before evaluations on Days 2 and 3.
If repeating the whole battery, wait ≥45 days between sessions or use a new set of animals.

steps.title: Conduct open field test
steps.instruction: Move the rat to the test room ≥1 h before testing in a quiet, dimly lit room (white noise optional), clean the open‑field arena, place the animal next to a wall, record locomotion for 9 min (first 3 min exploratory, next 6 min for motor assessment) using Videomex‑V, then remove the animal to a new cage, clean and dry the arena, and note fecal pellet count as an anxiety indicator.

substeps.instruction: Transfer rat to test room ≥1 h before test; ensure room is sound‑isolated, dim light, optional white noise.
Turn on recording apparatus/software; record session.
Clean arena to remove odors.
Place rat next to a wall (avoid center placement).
Record locomotor activity for 9 min (3 min exploratory, 6 min motor).
At end, move rat to a clean cage separate from other tested animals.
Disinfect arena with 30 % ethanol and allow to dry before next animal.
Count fecal pellets produced during the 9 min as an anxiety measure.

steps.title: Perform vibrissae test
steps.instruction: Acclimate the rat in the test room ≥1 h, clean the testing surface, set up video cameras beside and above the table edge, gently hold the torso, brush the vibrissae against the table edge to elicit an ipsilateral forelimb placement, count successful placements over up to 10 trials (exclude struggling trials), and return the animal to a new cage after testing.

substeps.instruction: Transfer rat to test room ≥1 h before test; ensure quiet environment.
Disinfect surface before and after test.
Turn on video cameras (side and top view).
Hold rat firmly by torso, avoiding obstruction of fore‑ or hind limbs.
Brush vibrissae against table edge to trigger forelimb placement.
Record each trial; count successful placements (max 10 events).
Exclude trials where the animal struggles.
After testing, place rat in a new cage separate from cage‑mates.

steps.title: Assess olfactory asymmetry
steps.instruction: One day before testing, habituate the rat for 10 min in a compartment with chocolate pellets placed at both ends while maintaining 90 % free‑feeding weight; on test day, after 1 h acclimation, place the rat in the testing corridor for 5 min, record video from above and front, count nose touches on the chocolate pellet (up to 20 touches or 5 min max), calculate % asymmetry = (contralateral touches / total touches) × 100, then move the rat to a new cage and disinfect the corridor.

substeps.instruction: Day ‑1 (habituation): expose rat to chocolate pellets in habituation compartment for 10 min; place pellets at compartment ends.
Maintain rat at ~90 % of free‑feeding weight.
Day 0 (test): transfer rat to test room ≥1 h before test.
Place rat in testing compartment; start 5‑min timer.
Turn on video cameras (top and frontal).
Count nose touches on chocolate pellet; stop after 20 touches or 5 min, whichever occurs first.
Calculate olfactory asymmetry %: (contralateral touches / (contralateral + ipsilateral touches)) × 100.
After test, move rat to a new cage.
Disinfect corridor surfaces before next animal.

steps.title: Execute uncoordinated gait test
steps.instruction: Acclimate the rat ≥1 h before testing, clean the beam, conduct a pre‑test on Day 2 using a 2 cm‑wide beam (place rat at lower end, encourage upward walk, assist with gentle hind‑limb pushes, two people help), repeat training on Day 3 with a 1 cm‑wide beam, and on Day 4 perform the final test on the 1 cm‑wide beam while recording video from side and front; measure slips (hind‑limb slides ≥1 cm off beam) and total walking time with a handheld timer.

substeps.instruction: Day 2 (pre‑test 1): move rat to test room ≥1 h before; clean thick beam (2 cm wide for rats).
Place new cage with sawdust at upper end, rat at lower end.
Encourage rat to walk upward; gently push hind limbs if needed; two experimenters assist.
Day 3 (pre‑test 2, 24 h later): repeat procedure using thin beam (1 cm wide for rats).
Day 4 (final test): clean thin beam, turn on side and front video cameras.
Place rat at lower end; record walk.
Count slips: hind‑limb slides ≥1 cm off beam.
Record total walking time with handheld timer.
Clean beam after each animal.

steps.title: Run cylinder test
steps.instruction: Acclimate the rat ≥1 h before testing, disinfect the cylinder, set up a video camera above it, place the rat inside and allow it to make 20 forelimb contacts with the wall (usually within 3 min), record the time needed, then calculate locomotor asymmetry % = (ipsilateral contacts + ½ simultaneous ipsilateral contacts) / total contacts × 100; after testing, move the rat to a new cage and clean the cylinder.

substeps.instruction: Transfer rat to test room ≥1 h before test.
Disinfect cylinder surfaces before and after test.
Turn on video camera above cylinder.
Place rat inside cylinder; start timer.
Record each forelimb contact with wall until 20 contacts are reached (typically ≤3 min).
Note time required to reach 20 contacts.
Calculate locomotor asymmetry % using provided formula.
After test, place rat in a new cage.
Disinfect cylinder before next animal.

steps.title: Perform forced swim test
steps.instruction: On Day 6 (pre‑test), transfer the rat to the test room ≥1 h before, fill a swim cylinder to 30 cm depth (rats) with water at 22–24 °C (monitor with mercury thermometer), place the rat individually for 15 min, then dry with microfiber towels, provide heat lamp, and house separately for 2 h; on Day 7, refill cylinder with water at same depth and temperature, record video from above and side, place rat for 5 min, then dry and return to cage.

substeps.instruction: Day 6 (pre‑test): move rat to test room ≥1 h before.
Fill swim cylinder to ~30 cm depth (rats).
Set water temperature to 22–24 °C; verify with mercury thermometer.
Place rat alone in cylinder for 15 min.
After 15 min, remove rat, dry with microfiber towels, give heat lamp.
If housed in group, keep rat in separate cage for ~2 h before re‑grouping.
Change water between each animal, keeping depth and temperature constant.
Day 7 (test): refill cylinder with water at same depth and temperature.
Turn on video cameras (top and side view).
Place rat in cylinder for 5 min; record behavior.
After 5 min, dry rat and return to cage.

description:
The methodology presented here allows performing and evaluating motor and non-motor behavioral alterations, resulting in an integral analysis of the PD model. Six different behavioral tests are described step by step and proposed to execute them sequentially, either in a single time or in a temporal course. To exemplify and validate the behavioral tests and show sensorimotor alterations, two different neurotoxins were used to generate independent parkinsonian rat models. We administered β sitosterol d- glucoside (BSSG) into the substantia nigra and 6-hidroxydopamine (6-OHDA) into the striatum. BSSG is a neurotoxin found in the plant Cycas micronesica
[1], which has been recently used to develop a PD model with construct, face, and predictive validity [2,3]. Meanwhile, 6-OHDA is the most widely used neurotoxin for modeling PD in experimental animals [4,5]. It should be emphasized that the behavioral tests validated here by using BSSG and 6-OHDA, are also suitable for parkinsonian rodent models induced by other neurotoxins such as rotenone [6], lipopolysaccharide (LPS) [7], and 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) [8]. Also for other pathological entities, in which movement disorders occur, such as the following: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis [9], Huntington's disease [10], cerebral stroke [11,12], intracerebral hemorrhage [13], and spinal injury [12]. The methodology of behavioral tests presented here underwent some modifications to the original protocol. Step 1: Unilateral intranigral or striatal injury by stereotaxic administration of a neurotoxin in the rat.
